During a 1929 excavation, of the ancient city of Uruk,
located in present-day Iraq, archaeologists unearthed
clay tablets inscribed with wedge-shaped writing.
The writing was identified as proto-cuneiform.
Dating back to 3100 BCE, this writing seemed
indecipherable. Also at Uruk, archaeologists found
shaped clay objects, each measuring only a few
centimeters, molded into shapes such as cones,
discs, and cylinders. These artifacts were also a
mystery; no one knew how or why they were used.
